about.text: Stilton is an English cheese, produced in two varieties: blue, which has Penicillium roqueforti added to generate a characteristic smell and taste, and white, which does not. Both have been granted the status of a protected designation of origin (PDO) by the European Commission, requiring that only such cheese produced in the three counties of Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire may be called Stilton. The cheese takes its name from the village of Stilton, now in Cambridgeshire, where the cheese was originally sold. Today, cheese made there cannot be named Stilton because of the PDO.

how.label: needle-pierce
how.text: Because the milled curd is never pressed, it settles with tiny airways between the pieces; the sealed surface keeps them closed until steel needles let air in at about six weeks and the Penicillium roqueforti starts veining from the centre. The cheese forms its own crust rather than having one applied.
